name: Gros Morne Mountain (James Callaghan Trail)
why: Up a gully of loose rock to the bare plateau of Newfoundland's second-highest peak, with arctic hares and caribou and the fjord of Ten Mile Pond below.
book: Park pass. The summit loop is closed from May to late June for caribou calving and when wet.
water: Stream at the base of the gully; none on the plateau.
dangers: Fog and cold wind on the plateau even in summer: the summit route is marked only by cairns.
Steep loose rock in the gully.
Long day: start the summit loop before 11:00.
turnaround: Do not start up the gully after 13:00 or in fog.

points.name: Gros Morne Mountain trailhead
points.note: A parking area on Route 430 near Rocky Harbour.

points.name: Base of the gully
points.note: A small pond and campsite where the steep climb starts.

points.name: Gros Morne summit
points.note: A flat stony plateau at 806 m, the summit cairn in the middle.

points.name: Ten Mile Pond lookout
points.note: The cliff edge over the landlocked fjord of Ten Mile Pond.

points.name: Back of the plateau
points.note: The long way down: round the back of the mountain over the tundra plateau and down a valley to the approach trail.
